issues.description: The problem UML and textual specification declare SealSaloon.orderMeal(Meal) as returning void, but the reference solution implements orderMeal(Meal) returning boolean. This is a method return-type mismatch that can confuse students about the required signature and cause test or compilation failures if automated tests expect a void method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent. Either update the solution to implement public void orderMeal(Meal meal) (keeping internal null checks but not returning a value), or update the problem statement and UML to indicate that orderMeal returns boolean. Preferably change the solution to the void signature to match the UML/specification so students implement the expected signature.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize both orders and stock in the SealSaloon constructor (explicitly: "These should be initialized ... in the constructor of SealSaloon"), but elsewhere in the same specification it mandates that the stock attribute must be static (shared across instances). Initializing a static stock in an instance constructor is contradictory and may mislead students about whether stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static field initialized elsewhere.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: state explicitly that orders is an instance field initialized in the constructor, and that stock is a static (class-level) final field that should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. Remove the ambiguous phrase suggesting stock be initialized in the instance constructor or change the static requirement if the intent is an instance stock.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) defines SealSaloon.orderMeal(Meal) with a void return type, but the solution implements public boolean orderMeal(Meal). This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation (placing an order) creates an API/expectation inconsistency: students reading the exercise and the UML expect a void method, while the reference solution returns a boolean. This can confuse students about the required signature, the expected usage, and may cause failing tests or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API so the method has the same signature across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the UML/problem by making orderMeal return void (public void orderMeal(Meal meal)) and remove the boolean return/adjust callers, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to specify boolean as the return type. Preferred fix: modify the solution to implement public void orderMeal(Meal meal) so it matches the documented specification.
